summary: Automated tests for the main-and-backup key switching, using a fake network layer so no real calls are made.
purpose: Checks that calls move to the backup key when the main one is spent or rejected, for the language model and the search providers.
why: Likely reason: the key chain logic is important for keeping the service working when a paid key runs out, so it has tests.
how: Before each test, it clears the key settings, sets the ones the test needs, and replaces the network fetch with a fake that records each call and returns a scripted answer. The tests then call the model and search clients and check the results.
inputs: The environment settings and the scripted fake answers defined inside each test.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test, shown by the Node test runner.
risks: The setup clears many environment variables and replaces the global fetch, so tests that run in parallel or do not restore these could interfere with each other.
debug: If a key test fails, check the fake answers in the setup for the status code returned, and check which key names were used in the recorded calls.
